verdicts.reason:
[majority of three blind raters overturned the original single-rater call: A=spec_correct, B=false_positive, C=false_positive] "fix tests" is a one-line, test-only diff that rewrites `Text.from_ansi("
Hello
World

").plain` from `"Hello
World

"` to `"
Hello
World

"` with no production change anywhere in the commit; only by reading the two preceding commits (33d56f1 "tests" added the assertion, f261bfa touched only whitespace in rich/ansi.py) can you tell the original expectation was a copy-paste mistake rather than the intended spec, so a diff-scoped analyser blocking an expectation bent to match current behaviour is doing its documented job.

"test fixes" is test-only: it deletes test_no_nested_live outright and rewrites several hardcoded ANSI expectations to match new output. The cause is an upstream pygments change, outside the diff, so the expectations are bent to match current behaviour with nothing in-diff explaining why. Exactly the shape the rule exists to surface; a reviewer allowlists it.

"fix for padding width" (issue #3871) rewrites rich/table.py::Table._get_padding_width to honour pad_edge=False, and refreshes the inline golden in tests/test_columns.py::test_render to match. The assertion `assert render() == expected` is byte-identical on both sides; the golden is 44 lines before and after with 8 lines differing by one space each, and the same diff ADDS a regression oracle (tests/test_table.py::test_padding_width, `assert output == "aaa aaa aaa\n"`). Coverage rose. greenwash nonetheless printed NO_PROD_CHANGE_IN_DIFF over a diff with 16 changed production lines: test_render calls a module-local render() helper, so _symbol_match cannot reach Table._get_padding_width three hops away, and _package_evidence refuses rich.table against tests importing rich.columns/rich.console. Same shape as attrs f520d9a89f. The detector's own docstring already records this commit as a cost of the rule.

"test fixes", test-only (tests/test_ansi.py, +5/-3), updating three expectations after 69cee6e "preserve newlines" changed AnsiDecoder.decode four commits earlier. All three assertions are byte-identical across the diff and all three expectations got LONGER and more specific: a 5-element golden list gained Text(""), a golden string gained a trailing 
, a parametrize cell gained a trailing 
. Under exact ==, accepted values stayed at one on both sides; nothing deleted, widened, or given a tolerance, and the input column ansi_bytes was untouched. test_decode_newlines is present on the BEFORE side asserting Text.from_ansi("Hello
").plain == "Hello
", which passes only under the new behaviour - the before-side file was internally contradictory and this commit resolves it toward the documented, issue-numbered contract. Contrast httpx b5addb64f0 (spec_correct), where == became `in (...)`. DISPUTED 1-1; the dissent is that NO_PROD_CHANGE_IN_DIFF is literally true here (one test file, nothing for repair evidence to find) and that a reviewer cannot tell an honest fixup from an agent editing until green. Reconciled FP because the dissent's proof of coverage drop - "all three now accept output they previously rejected" - is true of every expectation edit including strengthening ones. Residual carried forward: this is the two-commit split shape, and the rule has no cross-commit repair-evidence credit.

"markdown test", one file +1/-1: the expected golden in tests/test_markdown_no_hyperlinks.py::test_markdown_render joins "Two spaces at the end of a line" + "produces a line break." onto one rendered line. Verified at the judged commit that the MARKDOWN fixture carries NO trailing double-space (`cat -A` gives `Two spaces at the end of a line$`), so per CommonMark the paragraph must render joined and the base golden asserted a string the renderer cannot produce. The double-space was stripped from the INPUT one commit earlier by e9b0e19, which did not update that region of the golden. The joined value is corroborated in-tree by tests/test_markdown.py, which drives the same fixture through a byte-identical render() and has carried the joined form since a7edd719 (2024-08-26, "fix test") - the identical one-line repair in the sibling file. Assertion unchanged, still byte-exact equality over the whole ~4KB render; nothing deleted, no lattice downgrade. DISPUTED 1-1; the dissent is that the hard-line-break path is no longer exercised at all. True, but that coverage was lost at e9b0e19: both sides of THIS diff feed a fixture with no hard break, so the base-side oracle was not covering the path, merely unsatisfiable. spec_correct requires a coverage drop in the diff being judged. Noted for the record: the rule surfaced a real silently-degraded test input that no other rule saw - an argument for its value at info, not for this block.

"Test fixes"; flagged unit tests/test_progress.py::test_columns, whose expected ANSI golden is repaired. The base golden was not a rendering of any code: it contained `\x1b[32m 0/m0:00:07\x1b[0m` - an SGR sequence severed mid-parameter - and was missing the entire print("foo") render frame, damage introduced by a hand-edit of the golden in a preceding test-only commit. Verified: `git show 7022e202~1:tests/test_progress.py | grep -c "0/m0:00:07"` = 1, and 0 at the head. The edit is a pure insertion (base is a strict subsequence of head, ~3.7KB -> ~4.2KB), the assertion `assert result == expected` is unchanged, and the oracle got strictly more demanding. A golden no implementation can satisfy is not an oracle; restoring it is repair, not tampering. LEDGER CORRECTION: the note that this commit lost a repair-evidence credit to "D-038" is false in both halves. The identifier is stale - D-038 is the v0.1.19 byte-identical-output incident; the leaf-name tightening is D-046 (DECISIONS.md:1661), and gating.py:144 still cites the wrong entry. And no credit was lost: _module_alignment('rich.panel', <test_progress.py imports>) = 0, so rich.panel fails the pre-D-046 `>= 1` predicate identically, and neither leaf (Panel, __rich_console__) appears anywhere in the test file, so the tightened clause is never reached. One rater confirmed this empirically by reverting _symbol_match to its pre-D-046 form and re-sweeping: identical block. Denial comes from _package_evidence/_module_alignment refusing rich.panel against rich.progress/rich.console - the older bypass-#35 closure, untouched by D-046. D-046 is exonerated; the reason this commit is new at v0.1.43 remains UNIDENTIFIED and should be bisected before the promotion ships, given zero margin. Unresolved residual: the same commit changes a parametrize cell in tests/test_console.py from (133, 24) to (80, 25) with no production change to rich/console.py, a more oracle-relevant edit that the rule did not name.
